originalTitle: Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect

content: The European Union has ushered in some additional rules that aim to make it easier for people to identify chatbots and AI deepfakes online. The new transparency obligations under the bloc’s landmark AI Act came into effect on August 2nd, requiring companies to disclose when people are interacting with AI models, and if content has been generated or altered by them. The transparency rules differ between providers (companies that develop and market AI systems) and deployers (platforms and services that use those AI systems), though some companies like Meta and SpaceXAI are classified as both. [Image: If enough companies do adopt the EU’s AI icons then labels should look more consistent across online platforms. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-03-181006.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Providers must design AI systems to explicitly notify users when they’re dealing with AI instead of a human, “unless this is obvious,” and include machine-readable marks on synthetic audio, image, video, and text so that it can be detected as artificially generated or manipulated. Likewise, deployers are required to label any AI-generated or manipulated image, audio, and video deepfake content that’s designed to look real. “The rapid development of generative and interactive AI systems is making it increasingly difficult to distinguish AI interactions and AI-generated content from human-created and authentic content,” the European Commission said in its transparency guidelines. “People should know when they are interacting with AI or exposed to AI-generated content. This will help them make informed decisions, calibrate their trust and reliance on AI and avoid misinformation or deception.” The Commission has also developed a set of AI disclosure labels that tech platforms can adopt in accordance with the AI Act rules, alongside examples of when they should be used. These mirror similar labels that have already been introduced by TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook. The EU-made icons have been introduced to prevent platforms from having to design their own, and while the EU examples are optional to use, the Commission pointedly notes that its labeling requirements “are not.” [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Xtd8vhytuo] Companies that fail to comply with these new transparency rules risk facing fines of up to €15 million (about $17.2 million), or 3 percent of their global annual turnover. While the new transparency rules are enforceable immediately for new AI systems, any models and services that launched before August 2nd have a four-month grace period until December 2nd to comply.
chineseTitle: 欧洲 AI 标签和透明度规则现已生效
chineseSummary: 欧盟引入了一些额外的规则，旨在让人们更容易识别在线聊天机器人和人工智能深度伪造品。欧盟具有里程碑意义的人工智能法案规定的新透明度义务于 8 月 2 日生效，要求公司披露人们何时与人工智能模型交互，以及内容是否具有 […]
chineseContent: 欧盟引入了一些额外的规则，旨在让人们更容易识别在线聊天机器人和人工智能深度伪造品。欧盟具有里程碑意义的人工智能法案规定的新透明度义务于 8 月 2 日生效，要求公司披露人们何时与人工智能模型交互，以及内容是否由他们生成或更改。提供商（开发和营销人工智能系统的公司）和部署者（使用这些人工智能系统的平台和服务）之间的透明度规则有所不同，尽管 Meta 和 SpaceXAI 等一些公司被归类为两者。 [图片：如果有足够多的公司采用欧盟的人工智能图标，那么标签在在线平台上看起来应该更加一致。 https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-03-181006.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] 提供商必须设计人工智能系统，以便在用户处理人工智能而不是人类时明确通知用户，“除非这是显而易见的”，并在合成音频、图像、视频和文本上包含机器可读的标记，以便可以被检测为人工生成或操纵的。同样，部署人员需要对任何人工智能生成或操纵的图像、音频和视频深度伪造内容进行标记，使其看起来真实。欧盟委员会在其透明度准则中表示：“生成式和交互式人工智能系统的快速发展使得区分人工智能交互和人工智能生成的内容与人类创建的真实内容变得越来越困难。” “人们应该知道他们何时与人工智能互动或接触人工智能生成的内容。这将帮助他们做出明智的决定，调整他们对人工智能的信任和依赖，并避免错误信息或欺骗。”委员会还制定了一套人工智能披露规则
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
